entries.sense_en: the regular area or route that a police officer walks and watches

synonyms.nuance: The act of walking around to guard an area; beat is the fixed route or district itself.
A regular series of visits or stops, used for doctors, guards, milkmen; not police-specific.
synonyms.example: The doctor is on her rounds.

synonyms.nuance: An official administrative area; larger and more formal than one officer's beat.

entries.tip_ko: beat는 '때리다'만이 아니라 경찰의 '순찰 구역'이라는 뜻도 있습니다. a cop on the beat = 거리를 도는 순경.

entries.sense_en: a sudden, short, strong rush of wind

synonyms.nuance: A gentle, pleasant wind; a gust is sudden and forceful.
Stronger and more violent, often very cold or loud.
A sudden storm with strong wind, often with rain or snow, usually at sea.
synonyms.example: The boat was caught in a squall.

entries.sense_en: almost; very nearly

synonyms.nuance: The plain everyday word; well-nigh sounds old and literary.
Modern and a little formal; means 'in effect, for practical purposes'.
Informal and common in speech; often used for mild exaggeration.
synonyms.example: I practically ran all the way.

entries.tip_ko: nigh는 '가까운(near)'의 옛말입니다. well nigh impossible(거의 불가능한)처럼 지금도 가끔 문어체에 남아 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: spinning something round and round quickly, often with skill

synonyms.nuance: General word for turning fast; twirl suggests a light, playful or showy movement.
To turn or fiddle with something idly, often from boredom.
Faster and wilder, often with a sense of confusion or force.

entries.sense_en: down; along (an old poetic word)

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word; adown is archaic and used here for a mock-grand style.
Stresses following the length of something, without the sense of direction downward.

entries.tip_ko: O. Henry는 평범한 순경을 일부러 거창한 옛말(adown, pacific)로 묘사해 유머를 만듭니다.

entries.sense_en: a main road or street that people and traffic pass through

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for any road in a town; thoroughfare is formal and stresses passing through.
A wide city street, often lined with trees or big buildings.
A main road between towns or cities, for fast traffic.

entries.tip_ko: thorough의 발음 /ˈθɝoʊ/에 주의하세요. through(/θru/)와 모양은 비슷하지만 발음이 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: strong, solid and sturdy in build

synonyms.nuance: Neutral: strongly built; also used for furniture, shoes, etc.
Big, heavy and muscular; can sound rough or a little threatening.
Healthy and strong; often about health, systems or arguments, not just bodies.

entries.tip_ko: stalwart는 '충실한 지지자'라는 뜻의 명사로도 자주 씁니다 (a party stalwart).

entries.sense_en: a proud, confident way of walking that shows you think you are important

synonyms.nuance: A stiff, showy walk with the chest out; more ridiculous-looking than swagger.
A neutral or positive inner quality; swagger is how confidence shows outwardly, sometimes too much.
Clearly negative: believing you are better than others.

entries.sense_en: the area around a particular place; the neighborhood

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for the local area where people live; warmer and less formal.
General, neutral word for any region, big or small.
Formal: the state of being near, not the place itself.
synonyms.example: in close proximity to the station

entries.tip_ko: in the vicinity of ~ (~ 부근에)의 형태로 자주 쓰이며, 강세는 두 번째 음절 -ci-에 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: to go to bed and close up early; here, the shops and homes closed early
entries.sense_ko: 일찍 문을 닫다, 일찍 잠자리에 드는 생활을 하다

synonyms.nuance: A noun for a person who gets up early; keep early hours is about the whole daily routine.
The opposite: staying up or open until late at night.

entries.modern: went to bed early / closed early

entries.sense_en: sharp and quick to notice things

synonyms.nuance: Common and general; keen sounds a bit more literary and admiring.
Stronger: a look that seems to go right through you, often uncomfortable.
Awake and ready to notice danger; about a state, not a permanent quality.

entries.tip_ko: 영국 영어에서 keen은 주로 '열심인, 좋아하는'(I'm keen on tennis)이지만, 여기서는 '예리한'입니다.

entries.sense_en: a close friend (old-fashioned)

synonyms.nuance: Modern American informal word; the closest everyday equivalent.
Informal and friendly, slightly old-fashioned but still used.
Usually negative: a friend who gets favors, especially in business or politics.
synonyms.example: He gave jobs to his cronies.

entries.sense_en: wrote letters to each other regularly

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase; correspond is formal and suggests a regular exchange both ways.
synonyms.example: I'll write to you every week.

synonyms.nuance: Informal; any kind of contact, not only letters.
Broad and formal: any exchange of information by any means.

entries.tip_ko: correspond to ~ 는 '~에 해당하다'라는 전혀 다른 뜻이니, 전치사 with/to를 꼭 확인하세요.

entries.sense_en: to stop knowing where someone is or what is happening to them

synonyms.nuance: Specifically about stopping contact with a person; lose track of can also be about time or things.
Slowly becoming less close emotionally, not just losing contact.

entries.tip_ko: lose track of time (시간 가는 줄 모르다)도 아주 자주 쓰는 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: (informal American) a thing or situation to deal with; here, a huge place
entries.sense_ko: (구어) 상대해야 할 대상, 만만치 않은 것

synonyms.nuance: A formal suggestion or plan; proposition here does not mean a suggestion at all.
Neutral word for a subject or situation.
A big task or project someone takes on.
synonyms.example: Moving house is a big undertaking.

entries.modern: a big place / a whole different thing
entries.tip_ko: 보통은 '제안, 명제'지만, 여기서는 옛 미국 구어로 '(다루기) ~한 대상'이라는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: most loyal and dependable

synonyms.nuance: The usual modern spelling of the same word, especially for supporters and allies.
Everyday word; staunch adds firmness that does not change under pressure.
Stresses keeping promises and devotion over time; also used for marriage.

entries.tip_ko: 지금은 형용사로 staunch 철자를 쓰고, stanch는 주로 '(피를) 멈추게 하다'라는 동사로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a person who works slowly and steadily but without brilliance

synonyms.nuance: Positive; plodder hints at dullness or lack of talent.
Informal, about someone who is slow in general, often teasing.
Someone doing boring, hard work, often for others; more pitiful.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 plod는 '터벅터벅 무겁게 걷다'입니다. Bob은 친구를 약간 얕보며 말하고 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: (slang) a large amount of money; a fortune

synonyms.nuance: Standard word for great wealth; pile is casual slang.
synonyms.example: He made a fortune in oil.

synonyms.nuance: Informal, often for a large sum spent or earned at once.
Formal and general; describes being rich, not a sum you collect.

entries.modern: make a fortune / make a bundle

entries.sense_en: to be stuck in a fixed, dull routine that never changes

synonyms.nuance: The common modern idiom with the same negative meaning.
synonyms.example: I feel stuck in a rut.

synonyms.nuance: Positive modern slang: working or playing smoothly and well.
synonyms.example: The band was really in the groove.

entries.tip_ko: 요즘 in the groove는 오히려 '리듬을 타다, 잘 풀리다'라는 긍정적 의미이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

entries.sense_en: light rain made of very small drops

synonyms.nuance: A short fall of rain that may be heavy; drizzle is light and steady.
Tiny water drops hanging in the air, finer than drizzle.
The opposite: very heavy rain.
synonyms.example: We got caught in a downpour.

entries.sense_en: out and moving about

synonyms.nuance: Everyday: out and around; astir is literary.
Out of bed and active, often after illness.
Full of busy, noisy activity; astir can mean just a few people moving.

entries.tip_ko: a- + stir(움직이다)로 된 문어체 형용사로, 명사 앞이 아니라 뒤나 be 동사 뒤에 옵니다.

entries.sense_en: in a gloomy, miserable way

synonyms.nuance: Close in meaning; stresses dark, low mood.
synonyms.example: He stared gloomily out the window.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger personal unhappiness or discomfort.
synonyms.example: She shivered miserably in the cold.

synonyms.nuance: Stresses dullness and boredom more than sadness.
synonyms.example: The rain fell drearily all day.

entries.tip_ko: dismally failed(처참하게 실패했다)처럼 '형편없이'라는 뜻으로도 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: the state of being silly and unreasonable; almost to absurdity = almost ridiculously

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and often dismissive; used for ideas or talk.
Stresses that something invites laughter.
Literary; foolishness that leads to harm.
synonyms.example: It was folly to go out in the storm.

entries.sense_en: completely certainly; without any doubt

synonyms.nuance: British, humorous and old-fashioned version.
synonyms.example: He'll be late, sure as eggs is eggs.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral modern phrase, usable in any register.
synonyms.example: It's without a doubt the best.

synonyms.nuance: Means 'as expected'; used when a prediction comes true.
synonyms.example: Sure enough, it started to rain.

entries.modern: for sure / no doubt about it

entries.sense_en: (old American slang) excellent; very good

synonyms.nuance: The everyday modern word for the same enthusiasm.
Also a bit old-fashioned, more polite and upper-class.
Old American slang like bully, popular in the early 1900s.

entries.tip_ko: 지금 bully는 거의 '괴롭히는 사람, 괴롭히다'로만 씁니다. 여기서는 20세기 초 '최고야!'라는 감탄사입니다.

entries.sense_en: too much pride in yourself and love of talking about yourself

synonyms.nuance: Too high an opinion of your own abilities; less about talking.
Too much pride, especially in your looks.
synonyms.example: He checked the mirror out of vanity.

synonyms.nuance: In careful use: acting only in self-interest, not necessarily boasting.

entries.tip_ko: egotism(자기 자랑)과 egoism(이기주의)은 철자가 비슷하지만 뉘앙스가 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: almost hidden, as if sunk deep inside (his overcoat)

synonyms.nuance: Everyday: covered up completely; submerged comes from being under water.
General: not seen, with no image of sinking.
Informal image of being lost inside something big.
synonyms.example: He was swallowed up by the crowd.

entries.tip_ko: 원래 '물속에 잠긴'이라는 뜻을 비유적으로 써서, 얼굴을 숨기려는 인물의 모습을 암시합니다.

entries.sense_en: a very strong, bright light that is hard to look at

synonyms.nuance: Soft, steady and warm light; glare is harsh and strong.
Light so bright it blinds you for a moment; often admiring.
synonyms.example: the dazzle of the sun on the snow

synonyms.nuance: A small, shining light reflected from a surface.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 glare at ~은 '~을 노려보다'라는 뜻입니다. 여기서는 명사 '눈부신 빛'.

entries.sense_en: said something suddenly and sharply, in an angry way

synonyms.nuance: Louder, like giving an order; snap is short and sudden.
A quick, clever or angry reply to what someone said.
Low, rough voice showing anger or threat.

entries.sense_en: a short, flat nose that turns up at the end

synonyms.nuance: Same shape; a neutral description, less jokey than pug.
synonyms.example: a child with a snub nose

synonyms.nuance: The opposite in this sentence: a large nose with a high, curved bridge.
Small and round, usually said as a cute compliment.

entries.tip_ko: 퍼그(pug)라는 개의 얼굴처럼 납작한 코를 말합니다. Roman nose(매부리코)와 대비됩니다.
